managed_launch_notice: Approved component IDs are officecli, bun and node. Use component=officecli with literal args for managed Office file operations; use component=bun or component=node for their host components. Choose exactly one of component, command or cmd. The host resolves the verified executable and required environment; do not copy paths or environment from Skill resources. This host launch contract takes precedence over Skill reference text describing component-path lookup or ambient command invocation. Office operations are one-shot: do not open a resident session or start watch. Missing managed components are prepared automatically by the host; preserve its progress, cancellation and actual preparation failure. Do not substitute a same-named ambient program for an explicit component launch. This guidance grants no tools or permissions.

guides.description: Upload the requested local regular files through the observed file input or its actual native chooser. File sources use the current OS identity and accept native absolute paths or paths relative to the Session default directory, including parent traversal, legal links, Windows drive/UNC paths and mounted volumes. The default directory selects relative paths; it is not a local access limit. The host prepares stable snapshots preserving source names, bytes and modification time, then retains them while the browser may still hold File objects. Source changes or access failures require inspecting the actual cause before proposing a fresh call; do not automatically replay an uncertain browser transmission. An engine that does not implement Agent upload reports UnsupportedAction; this does not indicate missing system permission.

parameters.description: Exact local file sources: native absolute paths or paths relative to the Session default directory. Keep native separators and legitimate parent traversal; do not prepend the project display name. Legal links and mounted volumes resolve through native file handles.

guides.description: Read a local file or inspect instruction scope. Repository instructions are not ordinary text: never use the default text format for AGENTS.md or AGENTS.override.md. Their applicable bodies are injected separately after instruction discovery. Before reading a source file in any scope not already discovered, call read_file alone on its directory with format=instruction_scope (path=. for the workspace root; recursive=true only when needed); after that result, reconsider and send source reads with fresh call IDs. For format=instruction_scope, recursive controls descendant discovery and execution_identity selects this read operation identity; NEVER include missing_ok, offset, limit, start_line, line_count, or expected_sha256. Keep the same execution_identity for scope discovery and the corresponding instruction/source reads. Default format=text. For source inspection use start_line (1-based) and line_count (default 200), without offset/limit. A small file can be read with just path. Byte pagination remains available: bounded UTF-8 pages, source at most 8 MiB; offset reads are independent current-version observations. In every successful text result, sha256 always identifies the entire source and total_bytes is its full size, even when content is only one line/byte page and eof=false; do not read the whole file only to obtain its digest. To assemble consistent pages, follow next_offset with the prior expected_sha256 until eof; explicit hash mismatches still fail. Offsets/limit are bytes, not lines. FILE_CONTENT_CHANGED means discard prior pages and restart. Text-only missing_ok=true returns workspace_file_absent for genuine absence, never for denied access. format=image: PNG/JPEG/WebP at most 4 MiB, omit offset/limit/missing_ok and submit alone; requires an image-capable exact model route. Returns prepared pixels, not base64 text; images may be resized and must be re-read after history/compaction omitted pixels. Optional expected_sha256 guards text/image source versions. format=instruction_scope: metadata for a file or directory (path=. for workspace root). Optional recursive=true discovers descendant instruction directories, including hidden/ignored entries, within bounded limits. Check complete/incomplete_reasons and use canonical_path; incomplete is not absence. This is not a filesystem snapshot or proof of shell access scope. Native absolute paths and paths relative to the Session default directory are accepted, including parent traversal and mounted volumes. The default directory selects the project context, not a local access limit. System file access, privacy permission and administrator authentication follow the actual operating system. When this read actually requires system administrator filesystem identity, use execution_identity=administrator on this same read_file tool for text, image or instruction_scope, retaining the requested read format, page and source guard. The host uses the existing native system execution component. This remains read-only and does not grant file-write actions or change the frozen ToolPlan. A normal access denial is not proof that administrator identity is the remedy: independent privacy grants require their actual system interaction. missing_ok never turns denied access into absence.

Available for every format, including instruction_scope and all text/image pages. Keep identity consistent with the scope whose instructions are being discovered. Keep this value and execution_identity consistent across discovery and the operation.
One-based source line, with line_count; omit byte offset/limit. For the last N lines, first observe total L, then use max(1,L-N+1). A head-only page does not satisfy a requested tail read.
Number of source lines to inspect, still bounded by the response byte budget.
Byte offset, NOT a line number. For pagination use the exact prior next_offset and expected_sha256.
Byte budget, NOT a number of lines. Omit for normal reads; use line_count for source lines.
The whole-source SHA-256 returned by any successful text or image read. Use it to pin a later page or source version.

guides.description: Apply bounded, ordered, exact line hunks through the local file owner. Missing parent directories are created after the entire patch is validated. Prefer each file's expected_source={kind:existing,sha256:<full read_file digest>} or {kind:absent} after observing absence; this detects changes outside the hunk too. Omission/any uses line-only matching, not a source-version check. Never remove a rejected guard just to retry; re-read and replan. Supply logical text without CR/LF or a file-leading UTF-8 BOM; source BOM, unchanged line endings and EOF-newline policy are preserved, added lines use the first source ending (LF if none). For a one-line replacement use old_start=1, old_lines=1, new_start=1, new_lines=1 and lines=[{kind:remove,text:old},{kind:add,text:new}]. A context line is retained and counts in both old_lines and new_lines; context+add inserts after that line and does not replace it. Nonempty ranges are 1-based; old_lines=0 inserts after old_start source lines (0=BOF), new_lines=0 names the surviving output prefix. Context/remove text must match exactly; re-read on mismatch. All targets and source guards are prepared before writes, with per-file atomic publication and best-effort restoration of existing files, not a multi-file transaction. Failed patches may retain newly created files; inspect zero-based request.files indices in the failure observation and re-read every target before replanning/retrying. A restored result is historical, not a current-state lock. Concurrent native edits remain possible. Each file's written_sha256 identifies published bytes for a later guarded read_file or patch, not task completion. Native absolute paths and paths relative to the Session default directory are accepted, including parent traversal and mounted volumes. The default directory selects the project context, not a local access limit. System file access, privacy permission and administrator authentication follow the actual operating system. If an operation is denied, inspect the concrete cause and any partial effects; use the existing process execution path with the necessary execution_identity when appropriate, without blindly replaying completed work.

For replacement, lines must contain remove(old) then add(new). context is unchanged text and counts in both old_lines and new_lines; it does not replace itself. Schema keywords such as minItems/maxItems are not arguments.

guides.description: Run one local command as a Session-owned process with a bounded initial observation. This is the single launch tool for ordinary, long-running and interactive commands. The initial wait defaults to 1000 ms (0..30000); return either the actual terminal result or running with the exact process_id and retained output. Running means only that launch succeeded, never command completion or authorization. Do not launch again because a result is running. Read later output through the original owner; wait for genuine output or terminal changes without repetitive model polling. When output requires a human answer or external user action, show the actual needed information through request_user_input alone; the host closes the current Turn and retains the original process in this Session. After the user replies, inspect that same process_id; background output or exit does not create a new model call. A user saying done is not an authorization receipt: inspect the original process result. For immediate READY/input/EOF workflows use wait_ms=0,tty=false, then the exact authorized poll/input/close/poll controls. PTY is not pipe EOF. timeout_ms is an optional explicit hard execution deadline, distinct from the initial observation. Omit it when no actual task deadline is required, especially for human authorization. There is no default process deadline or idle expiration. An explicit deadline terminates and cleans up the original process on expiry; asking the user never extends it. Never use shell backgrounding, raw PID or temporary-log indirection, or split a live process across AgentExecution steps. Session-owned processes survive ordinary Turn closure, including user-input handoff, until they exit, are explicitly cancelled, reach an explicit deadline, or the Session is torn down. Process handles never survive application restart; user-requested persistent services must use and verify the platform native service facility. Choose exactly one target: approved component, literal command, or shell cmd. component and command take literal args arrays. For managed Office operations use component=officecli; for one ordinary executable use command plus args; use cmd only for shell syntax. Do not pre-read a user-specified executable or run ls/pwd/test preflights solely to launch it; the owner validates executable and cwd and injects applicable instructions. Use read_file/search_files for file contents and literal search, inspect truncation and errors, and never suppress stderr to manufacture an empty successful result. A zero exit only describes this command and does not prove the entire task. For a required administrator operation choose execution_identity=administrator; native authentication may need user action and does not grant unrelated desktop/privacy permissions. The following examples illustrate syntax only and authorize no extra actions.

parameters.description: Approved host component ID: officecli, bun or node. The host resolves its verified executable and required environment. Choose exactly one of component, command or cmd; pass each literal argument in args without shell quoting or expansion. Follow the managed launch notice for one-shot Office use and unavailable-component handling.
Shell-script form only: supply {"cmd":"script text"} and omit both command and component. Omit args for shell script text; never use cmd for an executable plus literal argument tokens.

host_os.windows: Runs script text directly through Windows PowerShell 5.1. PowerShell cmdlets such as Copy-Item, Move-Item, Remove-Item and New-Item are shell operations, not executables: use cmd, not command=Copy-Item or tokenized powershell.exe -Command arguments. For example {"cmd":"Copy-Item -LiteralPath 'a path/source.txt' -Destination 'a path/copy.txt' -ErrorAction Stop"}. Keep each quoted literal path in this script and preserve errors. Do not add mkdir when the accepted task says the directory already exists. Preserve native absolute or Session-default-directory relative paths without a project-name prefix. Do not prefix cmd with powershell.exe or pwsh. Do not assume PowerShell 7-only syntax such as ??, ??=, ?:, &&, or ||. Command Prompt syntax such as dir /b requires command=cmd.exe with args beginning ["/d","/c"]. Ordinary executables such as bun/git use command plus args. Never combine the forms.
host_os.macos: Use cmd only when shell semantics such as pipelines, redirection, globbing, compound syntax, or a shell script are required. Runs through /bin/sh -c on this process host. For an ordinary single executable use command plus args. Never combine the forms.
host_os.linux: Use cmd only when shell semantics such as pipelines, redirection, globbing, compound syntax, or a shell script are required. Runs through /bin/sh -c on this process host. For an ordinary single executable use command plus args. Never combine the forms.

parameters.description: Executable form: supply {"command":"program","args":[...]} and omit cmd and component. This field is the executable name or path only. Never include arguments such as git status in this field.

host_os.windows: Examples are git, bun, powershell.exe, or cmd.exe. PowerShell cmdlets such as Copy-Item and Move-Item need cmd script text, not a literal executable or tokenized -Command arguments.

parameters.description: Valid with command or component, never as shell arguments for cmd. Literal separate argument tokens as an actual JSON array value, never a JSON-encoded string. Omit when empty; do not send null. Quoting, wildcards, environment references and substitution text are passed literally for component/command.

host_os.windows: Examples: ["status","--short"] for git, or ["/d","/c","echo ready"] for command=cmd.exe. PowerShell cmdlets need cmd script text instead of tokenized -Command arguments.
host_os.macos: Examples: ["status","--short"] for git, ["-a"] for command=/bin/ls, or ["help","batch"] for component=officecli.
host_os.linux: Examples: ["status","--short"] for git, ["-a"] for command=/usr/bin/ls, or ["help","batch"] for component=officecli.

parameters.description: Native absolute directory or path relative to the Session default working directory. Omit cwd or use "." for the default. Parent traversal, platform-native separators, legal links, Windows drive/UNC paths on Windows and mounted directories are supported. The default directory is not a local access boundary.

Optional positive hard execution deadline in milliseconds from launch. The value must fit the native monotonic clock. Omit when the accepted task has no actual deadline; do not invent a deadline for human authorization. No default deadline or idle expiry applies. Observing, asking or replying never extends an explicit deadline; expiry terminates and cleans up the original process.

false (or omitted) uses pipe; true uses PTY. For a requested pipe stdin/EOF lifecycle use tty=false and wait_ms=0. PTY is not a substitute for pipe close_stdin. Either transport returns running after the bounded observation when the process remains live.

Initial observation window in milliseconds, default 1000, maximum 30000. A bounded nonzero initial wait is permitted; 0 admits immediately for READY/input/EOF workflows. Expiring this observation returns running with the original process_id and output, without killing the process or renewing timeout_ms. A task explicitly requesting a distinct poll still requires that poll.

Use current_user for ordinary execution; choose administrator only when the requested operation actually requires system administrator identity. The host uses the platform native authentication and execution path, preserving the real login user environment and task lifecycle. This selects this operation execution context, not a user permission mode. Administrator identity does not grant independent privacy or desktop permissions. Inspect partial effects before retrying a denied operation; never blindly replay an entire installation. Desktop, accessibility, screenshot, browser, media and Apple Events calls normally stay in the real login user App chain; an administrator service is not an interactive desktop and does not inherit the App privacy grants.

host_os.windows: The JSON field cmd is a Windows PowerShell 5.1 script, NOT cmd.exe. For workspace text and literal search, use read_file/search_files. Windows PowerShell 5.1 Get-Content without -Encoding can decode a BOM-less UTF-8 file as the local ANSI code page: correct hash/line counts do not prove correct decoded text. If a native shell read of a known UTF-8 file is required, use Get-Content -LiteralPath 'path' -Encoding UTF8 -Raw; use -Encoding UTF8 for Select-String too. Do not guess an unknown file encoding. Do not use cd && dir /a, &&, ||, ??, ??=, or ?: in that field. For the exact current directory use {"cmd":"(Get-Location).Path"}; plain Get-Location prints a table that can truncate the path. For root entries and their actual flags use {"cmd":"Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath . -Force | ForEach-Object { [pscustomobject]@{Name=$_.Name;Attributes=$_.Attributes.ToString();Hidden=[bool]($_.Attributes -band [IO.FileAttributes]::Hidden);System=[bool]($_.Attributes -band [IO.FileAttributes]::System);LinkType=$_.LinkType} } | ConvertTo-Json -Compress"}. Attributes is a flags enum: test each Hidden/System bit with a Boolean cast or compare the bitwise result to zero. FileAttributes.Normal is 128, not zero; comparing a masked Hidden bit to Normal incorrectly marks every entry hidden. Keep the shown Boolean-mask example. Include all returned names; describe Hidden/System only from those flags. A dot-prefixed Archive-only file is not hidden on Windows. A names-only listing cannot prove attributes. Do not recurse or follow links unless requested. For Command Prompt scripts use {"command":"cmd.exe","args":["/d","/c","cd & dir /a"]}. Do not prefix cmd with powershell.exe or pwsh. command plus args invokes a literal executable.
host_os.macos: cmd invokes /bin/sh -c; command plus args invokes a literal executable. For the physical current directory, use {"command":"/bin/pwd","args":["-P"]}. For a top-level listing including dot entries, use {"command":"/bin/ls","args":["-a"]}. These are executable forms; omit cmd. Do not put the entire command line in command. Omit . and .. from business entry counts.
host_os.linux: cmd invokes /bin/sh -c; command plus args invokes a literal executable. For the physical current directory, use {"command":"/usr/bin/pwd","args":["-P"]}. For a top-level listing including dot entries, use {"command":"/usr/bin/ls","args":["-a"]}. These are executable forms; omit cmd. Do not put the entire command line in command. Omit . and .. from business entry counts.

guides.description: Poll a Session-owned process from a bounded output cursor and observe its current state/cleanup evidence. For each following poll, copy the previous receipt's output.next_cursor into cursor and use wait_ms for bounded waiting. Omitting cursor means 0 and replays retained output; unread output returns immediately even with wait_ms=30000, so it cannot serve as a wait loop. After start_process, use poll_process with the exact process_id to wait for expected output before cancellation; do not infer readiness from a PID or temporary file. Report readiness once, then wait without repeating the same running-status narration. A terminal state=cancelled with cleanup.reaped=true is a successful poll observation, not a tool failure.

parameters.description: For a following poll, pass the previous output.next_cursor. Default 0 deliberately replays retained output; it does not resume at the last observation.

Per-poll wait in milliseconds, from 0 through 30000 inclusive. This is separate from the process lifetime timeout_ms: never copy a launch timeout such as 120000 here. Use 0 for an immediate observation, 1000 for a short wait, or 30000 for the longest allowed poll. Wait up to this duration for new output or terminal state. Retained output after cursor returns immediately. Advance cursor before waiting again; 0 only observes current state.
